pr.title: Replace locals in debuginfo records during ref_prop and dest_prop
pr.author: dianqk

processing.reason: The PR's historical defect is confined to debuginfo metadata, not executable MIR semantics. In the dest_prop diff, the pre-fix pass still computes the same return value: before, `_3 = copy _2; ... _0 = copy _3`; after, the `_3` assignment is nop'd and `_0 = copy _2`—semantically identical. The only stale records are `debug c => _3` and `// DBG: _3 = &_1`, which the fix remaps to `_2`. Likewise ref_prop only fails to remap `debug a => _1` / `// DBG: _1 = &(*_2)` to `_5`; the returned reference and all runtime assignments are equivalent. The added Validator check is a compile-time MIR/debuginfo validity check, not a change in program results. Therefore no ordinary Rust input can make the original and buggy-transformation functions produce different defined runtime values. Encoding the stale debug-local index as a return value would fabricate an unrelated semantic difference rather than model an executable miscompilation, which the task forbids.

analysis.originalLogic: When DestinationPropagation merges a local destination into a source local, or ReferencePropagation replaces a fully-replaceable SSA local with a reborrow target, the passes rewrite normal MIR statements/places/terminators and nop the eliminated assignments. Historically their visitors either returned early on a debug assignment (`statement.make_nop(true); return;`) or only rewrote `VarDebugInfo` places without tracking a local remap, leaving `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef`/`VarDebugInfo` records pointing at the original local (`debug c => _3; // DBG: _3 = &_1;` in dest_prop; `debug a => _1; // DBG: _1 = &(*_2);` in ref_prop).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The optimization eliminates/replaces local `_x` with `_y` in all executable MIR uses (and no longer emits the defining assignment to `_x`), but the debuginfo records `debug name => _x` and the `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef(_x, ..)` assignment are left unchanged, so debug records reference a local that is no longer in debuginfo/valid. Correct behavior remaps both the `VarDebugInfo` place and the `StmtDebugInfo` local to `_y`: dest_prop diff shows `debug c => _3;` / `// DBG: _3 = &_1;` becoming `debug c => _2;` / `// DBG: _2 = &_1;`; ref_prop diff shows `debug a => _1;` / `// DBG: _1 = &(*_2);` becoming `debug a => _5;` / `// DBG: _5 = &(*_5);`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR built with debuginfo enabled (`-g`) where a local referenced by a debug record is removed/replaced by DestinationPropagation (`Merger` over `merged_locals`) or ReferencePropagation (`Replacer` over SSA-replaceable reference locals / reborrow chains), including inlined functions with scoped debug locals.
analysis.summary: When local-replacement passes (DestinationPropagation, ReferencePropagation) eliminate/replace a local, all debuginfo records for that local—both `debug name => local` and `// DBG: local = ...` StmtDebugInfo assign-refs—must be remapped to the replacement local; otherwise debug records reference locals no longer in debuginfo. The fix also adds a Validator check and moves var_debug_info visiting before basic-block visiting in the MIR visitor.
analysis.trigger: A pass merges/propagates local `_x` to `_y` while a `VarDebugInfo` place or `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef` still names `_x`; e.g. dest_prop merges `_3` into `_2`, or ref_prop replaces SSA local `_1` with promoted local `_5` after inlining.
preconditions: Debuginfo is enabled (`-g`) so `body.var_debug_info` and StmtDebugInfo records exist.
DestinationPropagation has a local in `merged_locals` that also has a debuginfo record, or ReferencePropagation fully replaces a local whose debug place is visited.

In ref_prop, `remap_var_debug_infos` must be populated while visiting `VarDebugInfo` before `visit_statement_debuginfo` runs, requiring var_debug_info to be visited before basic blocks in the MIR visitor.
pitfalls: Rewriting only `VarDebugInfo` places is insufficient: `StmtDebugInfo::AssignRef`/`InvalidAssign` embed a bare `Local` that must also be remapped.

Calling `statement.make_nop(true); return;` on a merged-local debug statement skips visiting it, so its attached debug record is never remapped; the fix removes the early return and always calls `super_statement`.
Visitor ordering matters: var_debug_info must be visited before basic blocks so the remap table is ready when statement debuginfo is visited.
Borrowing restrictions (e.g. reborrow chains) and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions; do not conflate them when constructing the differing programs.
Validator should reject debuginfo records for locals not in `debuginfo_locals`, catching this class of stale-record bug.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation` and `//@ test-mir-pass: ReferencePropagation` with `-g` plus `-Zmir-enable-passes=+DeadStoreElimination-initial` (and `-Zub_checks=false -Zinline-mir` for ref_prop) and check emitted MIR diffs that the `debug <name> => <local>` and `// DBG: <local> = ...` use the same replacement local (dest_prop `_3`→`_2`, ref_prop `_1`→`_5`). Add `-g -O` `//@ build-pass` UI regression tests replicating issue #147485 (`dest_prop_debuginfo-147485.rs`, `ref_prop_debuginfo-147485.rs`). Construct two programs differing only in whether debuginfo is enabled and whether a debug-record local is later replaced/redefined, then compare emitted debug records; do not claim execution/reproduction.
evidence: +        // Ensure that debuginfo records are not emitted for locals that are not in debuginfo.
+            self.failures.push((location, format!("{local:?} is not in debuginfo")));
